video_title: Solana’s President on the Next Era of Crypto | with Lily Liu at Breakpoint 2026 in London
gist: Solana Foundation president Lily Liu (captioned 'Lily Louu') argues Solana is finance-first infrastructure for 'internet capital markets', citing live Samsung Wallet USDC integration (82M wallets) and a planned 2027 DTCC integration, and pitches tokenization as a fix for passive-index distribution inefficiency. She warns of 18 months of AI-driven security incidents and blames weak crypto prices on capital rotation into AI and mega-IPOs (SpaceX, Anthropic) rather than fundamentals.

themes.theme: Internet capital markets thesis and the ecosystem 'order of operations'

insights.claim: Lily Liu frames Solana's build-out as a sequence: ship the blockchain, then attract developers and applications that can make money, then bring assets (tokenization/RWAs) on chain, with the end goal being an economy rather than just a network.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Solana's current phase is asset onboarding; watch RWA/tokenized asset issuance metrics as the KPI of the strategy.
insights.quote: we're building an economy we're not just building a blockchain

insights.claim: Liu describes a spectrum of internet-native finance from the simplest use case (stablecoins and payments) to the most advanced (high-frequency trading of assets), with RWAs increasingly used as collateral in lending and borrowing markets in between.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: RWA-as-collateral in on-chain lending is the middle layer to watch for growth between payments and trading venues.

insights.claim: Liu argues the total addressable market for internet-native finance is ~5.5 billion internet users, versus ~1.5 billion for language-bound consumer internet products (English or Chinese speakers), because everyone uses money regardless of language.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Frames the bull case for payments/wallet integrations as a larger TAM than prior consumer internet waves.
insights.quote: what they have in common is not necessarily a language, but the fact that all of those five and a half billion people use money

insights.claim: Liu claims public blockchains will become home to the largest capital market — the internet capital market — because participants trade off almost everything else to be in the largest, most liquid market.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Liquidity network effects are the core moat thesis; favor chains with unified liquidity.
insights.quote: people would trade off practically everything else in order to be a part of the largest market

insights.claim: Liu says institutions that long preferred permissioned private chains are shifting to public blockchains, a shift she believes is still accelerating, because public chains offer net new users, distribution and liquidity beyond geographically bounded legacy infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Expect more TradFi tokenization launches on public L1s rather than private ledgers; a negative for private-chain vendors.

themes.theme: Samsung, DTCC and tokenized equities: TradFi distribution deals

insights.claim: Solana's Samsung partnership is live with Samsung Wallet in the United States, putting USDC natively into 82 million wallets.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: A large consumer distribution channel for USDC on Solana; watch on-chain USDC payment volumes and active addresses.
insights.quote: That's 82 million wallets that are using USDC built natively into the wallet.

insights.claim: The DTCC, which Liu calls the bedrock of US capital markets, is set to integrate Solana in 2027.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: A potential catalyst for tokenized equity settlement on Solana in 2027; track implementation milestones.
insights.quote: for the DTCC uh to be integrating Sana in 2027 is uh very meaningful

insights.claim: Solana has worked on tokenized equities for about a year and a half, starting as key partner on the xStocks launch with Kraken, and deliberately supports every tokenization model (transfer agent, RFQ, brokerage, SPV) and lets the market choose the standard.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Solana is hedging across tokenization standards; whichever model wins, it aims to capture volume.
insights.quote: we'll let the standards you know figure it out in the market which one is going to become the standard um but whatever that might be it's going to be on salon

insights.claim: Liu says Breakpoint 2026 drew so much interest from payments companies and Wall Street firms (e.g., Mastercard, Western Union, Barclays on the agenda) that the team describes it as 'Comic Con meets Milken'.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Signal of TradFi engagement with Solana; watch for concrete deployments, not just speaking slots.
insights.quote: It's like Comic Con meets Milkin.

insights.claim: Liu says firms like Samsung and DTCC are ultimately convinced not by technology pitches but by the prospect that Solana helps them grow their business, built through years-long relationships led by Solana's institutional and APAC leads.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Enterprise deals are slow, relationship-driven; announcements lag multi-year groundwork.
insights.quote: no one is bigger than the market

themes.theme: Tokenization as a fix for passive-index distribution inefficiency

insights.claim: Liu argues tokenization's real problem-solving value is distribution: with upwards of ~60% of US equity allocation passive, companies outside major indices like the S&P 500 are 'not on the escalator' and their cash flows are not fully valued, regardless of business quality.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Implies mid/small caps outside indices could benefit most from tokenized global distribution; a potential re-rating mechanism for underfollowed equities.
insights.quote: if you're not in the 100, if you're not in the 500, then you're not on the conveyor belt, you're not on an escalator

insights.claim: Liu compares blockchain capital markets to Uber: just as mobile phones enabled discovery and clearing of latent rider/driver demand, internet capital markets can match mid- and long-tail investment demand with undiscovered, not low-quality, assets.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Look for long-tail asset issuance and secondary liquidity as the evidence the thesis is working.

themes.theme: Finance-first architecture and Solana's competitive positioning

insights.claim: Liu says the key difference between ecosystems is whether a chain is a tech platform superpowered by finance (the Web3 'read, write, own' thesis) or financial infrastructure superpowered by technology, and Solana is finance-first, which drives its architectural choices.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Use this lens to compare L1 strategies; finance-first chains should prioritize liquidity and trading UX over general-purpose app features.

insights.claim: Solana chose no sharding and a single mainnet to keep unified liquidity, and Liu says if you build on the SVM it is Solana, unlike ecosystems with many teams building separate execution environments.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Contrasts with fragmented L2/rollup ecosystems; unified liquidity is the claimed moat.
insights.quote: If you're building SVM, it's Sana. If you're building a Sana, it's SVM.

insights.claim: Liu describes Solana's ambition as an 'API for capitalism', openly embracing helping participants make money as part of its culture.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Positioning targets financial apps and builders seeking monetization.
insights.quote: API for finance, API for capitalism

insights.claim: Liu reinterprets past crypto waves as finance: ICOs were v0.1 on-chain capital formation (which she expects to return), NFTs were markets around JPEGs, and blockchain gaming succeeds only when it adds payment rails and in-game item markets rather than running game back ends on chain.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Expect a return of on-chain capital formation; judge crypto-gaming projects by payments/markets integration, not on-chain compute.
insights.quote: ICO is essentially capital formation onchain for cryptonative projects

insights.claim: Asked whether the future is Solana-only or multi-chain, Liu answered 'Solana primarily'.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: The foundation is not positioning for a multi-chain hedge.

themes.theme: AI-era security risk for crypto and financial infrastructure

insights.claim: Liu predicts a 'pretty tough next 18 months' of AI-driven security incidents hitting financial and transportation infrastructure, with the blockchain industry front and center.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Raises hack/exploit tail risk for DeFi protocols; favor security-hardened protocols and price in exploit risk.
insights.quote: it's going to be a pretty tough next 18 months for really everybody

insights.claim: Liu says the industry must shift away from 'move fast and break things' for the next year or two to get security right, because the risk function in the age of AI is different than even six months ago (a Type I vs Type II error reorientation).
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Expect slower shipping and more security spending across crypto; possible tailwind for security/audit providers.
insights.quote: It's just a different risk function these days than it was even six months ago.

themes.theme: Crypto price weakness explained by capital rotation to AI and mega-IPOs

insights.claim: Liu attributes crypto's poor price action to asset-class allocation, not fundamentals: over the last couple of years risk and innovation capital rotated into AI, and blockchain periodically cycles from top to bottom of the frontier-tech pile.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Crypto prices may decouple from fundamentals during AI capital cycles; watch for rotation back as a catalyst.
insights.quote: clearly what happened over the last couple of years is all of that risk and innovationoriented capital went into AI

insights.claim: Liu says crypto hit similar price lows in the week before the SpaceX IPO and again one week before the Anthropic IPO, and believes investors are currently selling Bitcoin, SpaceX positions and frontier tech to fund Anthropic IPO allocations, with blockchain the biggest pile drained.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Mega-IPO funding can create temporary crypto selling pressure; potential buying opportunity after IPO liquidity events.
insights.quote: people are uh are liberating cash in order to fund their uh their allocation request for the anthropic IPO and that's all coming out of risk capital

insights.claim: Liu notes that about a year earlier there was intense exuberance around digital asset treasuries (DATs), followed by the typical crypto overcorrection.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: DAT unwind contributed to drawdown; be cautious of crypto-treasury company premiums.

insights.claim: In rapid fire, Liu called AI a 'friend' rather than foe of crypto.
insights.speaker: Lily Liu (President, Solana Foundation)
insights.so_what: Indicates the Solana Foundation sees AI as complementary despite the capital competition and security risks.
